title: Collateral Protection Insurance Servicing Standard — Insurance Tracking Held per Contract
content:
Collateral Protection Insurance tracking is held per contract, not per borrower. Every contract the company books opens one insurance tracking record on its contract date, so a borrower holds as many tracking records as they have financed vehicles. There is no per-borrower limit on the number of tracking records.

A contract never has more open tracking records (records not closed) than the product's limit on open tracking records per contract. A new tracking record is opened for a contract only after its previous record closed, and only for a reinstated contract whose record had closed.

## The standard in practice

| Situation | Tracking records |
|---|---|
| A borrower with one financed contract | one record, opened on that contract's contract date |
| A borrower with three financed contracts | three records, one per contract, each opened on its own contract date |
| A contract whose record is open | no second open record for that contract |
| A reinstated contract whose earlier record had closed | a new record may be opened, the earlier one having closed |

**Is there a cap on how many tracking records one borrower may hold?** No. Records follow contracts, and no per-borrower limit applies.

**Hypothetical:** a borrower with two financed vehicles, one booked on a hypothetical day 1 and one on day 90, holds two tracking records, opened on day 1 and on day 90.
